title: Pentagon declassifies new UFO files: do they prove extraterrestrial spacecraft exist?
excerpt: A new batch of Pentagon UFO files has been released, including documents, videos and reports. The result is clear.
content:
This is the sixth release of declassified documents under the PURSUE programme, bringing together material spanning more than seven decades, from 1952 to 2025.

The new release contains 71 files, including 55 PDF documents, 15 videos and one audio recording. Most of the material comes from the United States Department of Defence, although it also includes four videos submitted by law enforcement agencies in Colorado.

The documents contain a mixture of historical cases, recordings made by military sensors, sighting reports and documentation relating to former research programmes. However, the release does not in itself confirm that the phenomena observed are of extraterrestrial origin.

A new collection of UFO files

The sixth release was published on 18 September 2026 as part of PURSUE, the system created to facilitate the gradual publication of historical documentation relating to UAP.

According to information published by the Department of Defence itself, new releases will continue to be added to the archive progressively. The fifth batch was published on 7 August, meaning this latest release maintains the collection's regular update schedule.

Among the most striking materials are videos recorded by military platforms in different parts of the world, as well as historical documentation dating back to the early years of official US investigations into UFOs.

Luminous spheres above a military platform

One of the most striking videos in the new collection was recorded in 2025 using an infrared sensor installed on a US military platform.

The footage shows six small, apparently spherical objects grouped together in the sky. The military report describes them as objects that appeared agile and changed direction frequently.

The observer estimated that they could have been travelling at around 480 miles per hour, approximately 770 kilometres per hour.

The incident remains classified as unresolved. The fact that an object is classified as a UAP means that its nature could not be definitively determined using the available data, not that it has been established to be an extraterrestrial spacecraft.

Other videos recorded by the military

The new collection also includes recordings obtained by infrared sensors during military operations in different areas.

One of the cases concerns a 2022 incident in the Middle East, in which several objects were observed at different altitudes and speeds. The associated report states that the objects could have been between one and two metres in size and appeared to move irregularly.

Another of the videos shows several objects grouped together and moving as a formation.

This type of footage is particularly interesting because it comes from sensors used during military operations rather than solely from recordings made with mobile phones or conventional cameras. Even so, the images alone do not make it possible to determine what the observed objects were.

A 1952 audio recording brings Project Blue Book back into focus

Perhaps one of the most interesting documents from a historical perspective is an audio recording made in 1952 by Captain Edward J. Ruppelt, a US Air Force officer who would later lead Project Blue Book.

In the recording, Ruppelt explains the investigations the US Air Force was carrying out into UFO reports.

At the time, the investigation had accumulated hundreds of reports, some of which remained unexplained. According to Ruppelt in that presentation, around 20% of the cases they had studied could still not be resolved using the information available.

Ruppelt would later become one of the best-known figures associated with Project Blue Book, the US Air Force programme that investigated UFO sightings between 1952 and 1969.

The inclusion of this recording in the new collection makes it possible to hear directly from a key figure from the early stage of official investigations into unidentified aerial phenomena.

What do UFOs have to do with wormholes?

Another aspect generating considerable attention is the documentation relating to concepts such as wormholes, warp-drive propulsion, antigravity, negative mass and invisibility systems.

The documentation comes from a research programme run by the Defence Intelligence Agency known as the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP), which was created in 2008 and ended in 2012.

The sixth release includes 37 Defence Intelligence Reference Documents (DIRD) produced as part of that programme.

Their titles may seem surprising, but there is an important distinction: the documents themselves are described as reference and synthesis studies, and their publication does not mean that the technologies studied were developed or that the United States possesses spacecraft capable of using wormholes or warp-drive propulsion.

In other words, the fact that an official document examines a particular technological possibility does not mean that the technology currently exists.

A report on possible injuries linked to anomalous phenomena

The documents also include a 2010 technical study focusing on several cases involving people who reportedly suffered injuries following events considered anomalous.

The report examines three specific cases and describes physical symptoms recorded afterwards, as well as comparing them with known incidents involving radio-frequency exposure.

The document puts forward hypotheses about possible advanced aerospace systems, but does not conclusively identify the source of the exposures or demonstrate that those affected had been in contact with extraterrestrial technology.

Four videos recorded by police officers in Colorado

The new release also contains four videos from law enforcement agencies in Colorado, recorded in October 2023.

According to the published documentation, one officer described the phenomenon as silent, with flashing red, blue and green lights.

The footage was captured on mobile phones and is now part of the official UAP archive.

This type of testimony once again highlights one of the main problems when studying anomalous phenomena: an observation can be recorded and still remain unidentified when there is insufficient information about distance, size, speed, trajectory or atmospheric conditions.

Do these files prove that extraterrestrial spacecraft exist?

No.

The new declassification is interesting because it provides access to documentation that remained in government archives for years and brings together cases spanning more than 70 years. However, none of the published material constitutes proof in itself that UAP are spacecraft of extraterrestrial origin.

In fact, a significant proportion of the documents consists of investigations, technical reports or cases that remain unresolved because there is insufficient information.

The distinction is important: “unidentified” does not necessarily mean “extraterrestrial”.

The collection provides a better understanding of what military personnel observed, what US agencies investigated and which phenomena they were unable to identify using the available data. It also provides historical material that can now be analysed by independent researchers.

And the story is not over yet.

The Department of Defence has announced that it will continue publishing new files progressively, meaning this sixth release could be just another chapter in a much broader declassification effort.

Attention will now turn to the next documents and, in particular, to whether future releases provide sufficiently complete instrumental data to resolve some of the cases that remain open.

Source: NASANET
